signals.signal: Mandatory cashless acceptance for any purchase over EUR 1 came INTO FORCE 01/05/2026 (postponed from 01/03/2026 by parliament on 13/02/2026, under the amended cash-register/eKasa law adopted 21/10/2025). A merchant may comply with a card terminal, a dynamic eKasa QR code, or the state-built 'Notifikator okamzitych platieb' (NOP) instant-payment notifier (Financna sprava + Slovak Technical University; closed pilot 01/11/2025, public pilot Jan-2026). Banks may not charge notification fees until end-2027. Plain language: every shop, cafe and tradesman in Slovakia that takes cash must now also take a non-cash payment.
signals.implies: Nationwide acceptance land-grab: Verifone/Castles POS terminals for higher-volume merchants, softPOS on merchant smartphones for micro-merchants, and TMS to manage a suddenly much larger, more fragmented terminal estate. Also an opening to sell acquirers estate-monitoring and remote key injection (Thales HSM/RKI) as the fleet scales.
signals.likelihood: Certain - already in force; estate build-out runs through 2026-2027
signals.followup: Pull the exact amending act number from Zbierka zakonov / slov-lex; ask SK acquirers (SLSP/GP tom, VUB, ČSOB, Tatra) for terminal-deployment volumes and TMS gaps

signals.entity: Slovenska sporitelna / Tatra banka / CSOB SK / UniCredit SK / VUB banka
signals.signal: Slovak branch cash desks are being dismantled at scale. As at 28/07/2026: Slovenska sporitelna 93 of 128 branches operate WITHOUT a cash desk; Tatra banka 48 of 69 contact points; CSOB 47 of 120; UniCredit Bank 16 of 47; VUB banka 25 of 121 (the most traditional). Cash is being pushed onto self-service recyclers and ATMs in or beside the branch for 24/7 deposit and withdrawal, and teller staff redeployed to advisory. Plain language: 'recycler' = a machine that takes in notes and pays the same notes back out, so a branch needs far fewer cash deliveries.
signals.implies: Direct fit for Glory/Sesami TCRs and NCR recyclers, self-service lobby kiosks, x-core multivendor software and device telemetry/monitoring; VUB (only 25/121 converted) and CSOB (47/120) are the biggest untapped conversion pipelines.
signals.likelihood: High - programme visibly running at all five banks
signals.followup: Approach VUB and CSOB SK cash-operations/branch-transformation owners with a per-branch recycler business case; confirm incumbent device vendors

signals.entity: KBC Group / CSOB SR / 365.bank (incl. Postova banka)

Daniel Kollar was appointed CEO of 365.bank while remaining CEO of CSOB SR; the stated next step is a legal AND operational merger of 365.bank (with Postova banka and its Slovak Post distribution partnership) into CSOB. signals.likelihood: High - merger work starts in the 6-12 month window
signals.followup: Get the announced legal-merger date and combined ATM/branch counts from CSOB SR; target integration programme sourcing

signals.entity: Hungary - MNB / Act XVIII of 2025 (ATM mandate)
signals.signal: Phase 2 of the Hungarian ATM mandate has a HARD DEADLINE of 31/12/2026: every settlement with 500-1,000 residents must have at least one working ATM (phase 1, settlements over 1,000, closed 31/12/2025). Per-bank allocation under MNB Decree 19/2025 (VI.26.) is now public: OTP Bank 428 ATMs (~HUF 1.7bn), MBH Bank 195 (~HUF 780m), K&H 117 (~HUF 468m), Erste Bank Hungary 104 (~HUF 416m) - roughly 1,039 ATMs and ~HUF 4.156bn of investment. Banks may swap or take over each other's settlement packages, with swap contracts due by 28/02/2026. A separate government decree (Magyar Kozlony 29/05/2025, in force 07/06/2025) permits removal/relocation of an existing ATM only if at least one working ATM remains in the settlement or the unit moves to an underserved area.
signals.implies: A dated, mandated ATM procurement window closing 31/12/2026. NCR dispense ATMs plus x-core multivendor software, physical ATM security for unattended rural sites, telemetry/monitoring for a dispersed low-traffic estate, APTRA OptiCash cash optimisation (rural low-volume ATMs are exactly where cash forecasting saves money), and managed/field services across 1,000+ remote locations.
signals.followup: Confirm how many of the 1,039 are already installed as of Q3-2026 and which banks are behind; the OTP 428 figure was not in the baseline

signals.entity: OTP Bank Nyrt. and other Hungarian credit institutions
signals.signal: OTP Bank, joined by several other Hungarian credit institutions, filed a constitutional complaint (alkotmanyjogi panasz) with the Hungarian Constitutional Court on 10/11/2025 against Act XVIII of 2025, arguing the forced ATM installation and the MNB's allocation of machines is economically unjustified, disproportionately restricts the right to conduct business and to property, and discriminatorily distorts the market. No ruling reported as of 31/07/2026. [Regulatory risk to the ATM programme above - it does NOT suspend the 31/12/2026 deadline.]
signals.implies: A live legal challenge means banks will prefer cheap, fast, low-commitment ATM deployments and managed-service/opex models over capex-heavy purchases - which favours Printec's managed-services and ATM-as-a-service pitch over outright hardware sales.
signals.likelihood: Medium - ruling could land inside the 18-month window
signals.followup: Monitor alkotmanybirosag.hu for the case number and decision; check whether any bank has slowed installs pending the ruling

signals.entity: Hungary - national ATM estate (MNB Q1-2026 data)
signals.signal: Driven by the mandatory installation programme the Hungarian ATM estate hit a new peak: 5,688 ATMs operating nationwide at end-March 2026, nearly 500 more than a year earlier. Q1-2026 withdrawals: 18.5 million transactions worth HUF 2,293bn, average withdrawal HUF 124,179. The MNB's stated 2023 target was to grow total ATM stock by 52% by 2026.
signals.source_name: Mosthir.hu, citing MNB Q1-2026 payments data
signals.implies: ~500 net new ATMs a year in a single 10m-population market means sustained demand for ATM hardware, x-core multivendor software licences, cash forecasting (OptiCash) and field maintenance - Printec's managed-services 500+ engineer model is the natural fit for a rural estate.
signals.followup: Pull the MNB payment-systems report primary table for the ATM/deposit-ATM split

signals.signal: MBH Bank completed its 2025 Act XVIII ATM installation obligation ahead of the 31/12/2025 deadline (finished early December 2025), deploying 77 ATMs in 2025. It now runs the second-largest Hungarian network: ~1,200 ATMs at 1,114 locations. Its remaining phase-2 obligation is 195 ATMs by 31/12/2026. [Baseline knew MBH 195; the 1,200/1,114 estate size and the 77 2025 installs are new.]
signals.implies: A 1,200-unit estate at 1,114 sites (i.e. mostly single-ATM sites) is a strong telemetry/monitoring, cash-optimisation and field-service target; the 195 phase-2 units are near-term hardware plus physical ATM security.
signals.followup: Portfolio.hu article is partly paywalled - operator to pull full text for the 2026 install plan

signals.signal: qvik - the MNB's QR-code/NFC/deep-link payment scheme riding on the domestic instant payment system, live since 01/09/2024 and free by law for consumers - is scaling fast: 421,000 transactions worth HUF 17.1bn in Q3-2025, an eightfold rise in count and more than twelvefold in value versus Q4-2024, with average ticket up from ~HUF 23,000 (June) to over HUF 40,000 (September). Praktiker became the first retail chain to roll qvik out across its entire national network; Prima supermarkets and the Dijnet bill platform have joined. OTP, CIB and Erste support it. Acceptance is NOT mandatory for merchants (only electronic acceptance generally is, for online-cash-register merchants, since 2021).
signals.implies: Every qvik acceptance point still needs a POS terminal capable of displaying the QR/handling NFC, or a softPOS app - a terminal-refresh and TMS-configuration driver across the Hungarian acquiring estate, and a fraud-monitoring driver (instant, irrevocable payments).
signals.followup: Get the MNB Payment Systems Report 2026 for the current qvik acceptance-point count

signals.entity: Ceska sporitelna + CSOB + Raiffeisenbank (Czech Banking Association)
signals.signal: 'Vklad na kartu' - a shared deposit-ATM network across Ceska sporitelna, CSOB and Raiffeisenbank - lets a customer of any of the three deposit cash at any of the others' deposit ATMs, across MORE THAN 1,000 deposit ATMs nationwide. Piloted from early June 2025 on several dozen ATMs (3,000+ customers, average deposit CZK 11,000-15,000), live in production from 16/09/2025, and still being publicised/expanded as of 22/07/2026. The technical solution is a Mastercard/Visa international standard being trialled in the Czech Republic FIRST IN THE WORLD (Mastercard virtual/digitised cards from day one, Visa 'in the following months'). Deposits credited typically within one minute, max 30. CSOB and Raiffeisenbank charge nothing at partner ATMs, Ceska sporitelna CZK 40. CSOB limits: CZK 350,000 per transaction, CZK 700,000 per day. CSOB is growing its deposit-ATM count by about a fifth a year and operates 239 deposit ATMs. [STANDING - dated 2025 for the launch; the 22/07/2026 coverage and continued expansion are the current trigger.]
signals.implies: Interbank cardholder deposit demands multivendor ATM application software (x-core) able to run a common deposit flow across three different hardware fleets, plus intelligent-deposit/recycling hardware, device telemetry (an out-of-service shared ATM now fails three banks' customers) and cash forecasting. It is also a template Printec can carry to HU/SK/SEE.
signals.likelihood: High - live and expanding; other CZ banks likely to join
signals.followup: Get per-bank deposit-ATM counts and find out which ATM software vendor implemented the shared flow

signals.entity: Slovakia - Eurosystem / ECB digital euro pilot
signals.signal: The ECB announced on 14/07/2026 that it has selected 36 payment service providers for the digital euro pilot, from over 50 applications following a March-2026 call for expressions of interest. The pilot runs at the ECB and 19 national central banks INCLUDING Narodna banka Slovenska, starting in H2-2027 for 12 months. Named selected participants include UniCredit, Raiffeisen Bank International, Deutsche Bank, Revolut, Nexi Payments, Worldline and Poste Italiane. The ECB press release itself does not enumerate all 36, so NO specifically Slovak PSP could be confirmed from the primary source. Hungary and Czechia are outside the euro area and therefore outside this pilot.
signals.implies: Digital-euro readiness in Slovakia will hit POS terminals (offline/online acceptance), ATMs (digital-euro cash-in/cash-out at the ATM is an explicit Eurosystem use case), HSM/key management and wallet onboarding/eKYC. UniCredit and RBI both have Slovak subsidiaries (UniCredit Bank CZ+SK, Tatra banka) - the pilot work will land locally.
signals.likelihood: Medium - pilot starts H2-2027, preparation spend begins 2026-27
signals.followup: OPERATOR: pull the full 36-PSP list from the ECB digital euro pilot webpage (https://www.ecb.europa.eu/euro/digital_euro/pilot/html/index.en.html) and check for Tatra banka / UniCredit SK / VUB / SLSP

signals.signal: From November 2026 Czech banks will be obliged to accept only structured (ISO 20022) or hybrid addresses in payment instructions; batch instant payments for corporates are planned from 2026; SEPA instant payments in euro become mandatory across Europe from July 2027. The CNB-operated CERTIS Instant Payment Service carries Czech instant payments with a system limit of CZK 2,500,000 per payment in 2026. Plain language: ISO 20022 is the modern message format that replaces free-text address fields with separate street/city/country fields, so every payment-initiation and corporate file interface has to be reworked.
signals.implies: A dated payments-rail deadline (Nov-2026, then Jul-2027) forcing ISO 20022 message and corporate-file remediation - Printec's instant-payments/ISO 20022 practice, plus knock-on sanctions/AML screening changes when address data becomes structured (IMTF Siron / FICO).
signals.followup: Confirm the exact November-2026 obligation from a CNB primary page or EPC rulebook rather than the vendor explainer used here
